lots.guide_summary: Range is from 5 close SOLD Gowans hammers for plain 18ct bands of 2.0g to 3.0g ($250 to $390, Dec 2025 to Sep 2026), plus 1 close UNSOLD (2.1g passed in after 8 bids). No asking entries survive. Heavier bands of 3.2g to 3.9g made $360 to $500 (category guide). Plain 18ct bands at Gowans run about $125 to $150 per gram hammer. Melt check (a floor, not a sale): gold US$4,151.90/oz at 2026-10-14 08:28 UTC (api.gold-api.com) x 1.4328 AUD/USD (open.er-api.com) = about $191/g pure, $143.5/g at 18ct, about $359 for 2.5g.
lots.working: Keep: the close sold bands differ in weight, so I compare per gram. Lowest close result per gram is $125/g (lot 438645, 2g, $250, Sep 2026). 2.5g x $125 = $312.50 lowest same-item equivalent; $312.50 / 1.198 = $260.85, round down to $260 (all-in $311.48, below the $359 melt). Strictly unadjusted, the lowest close sale is $250 for a lighter 2g ring, giving $250 / 1.198 = $208.68, so $205; I use the weight-adjusted $260 because the comparables are lighter. Flip: likely resale about $330 hammer (2.5g x about $130/g, the middle of the recent per-gram sales), less an assumed 15% vendor commission ($49.50) and $0 postage (local resale) = $280.50; / 2.396 = $117.07, round down to $115. Selling to a scrap buyer at about 85% to 90% of melt ($305 to $323) gives a similar figure. Flip margin is thin, so KEEP only.
